verses.text: So you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge someone else. When you judge another person, you condemn yourself, because you who judge do the same things.
We know that God's judgement against people who do such things is based on truth.
Do you think, you who judge people for doing these things while you do the same, that you will escape God's judgement?
Or do you look down on the riches of his kindness, patience and long-suffering? Do you not realise that God's kindness is meant to lead you to turn back to him?
But because you are stubborn and will not turn back, you are storing up anger for yourself on the day of God's anger, when his just judgement will be shown.
God "will pay back each person according to what they have done."
He will give eternal life to those who keep doing good and seek glory, honour and a life that never dies.
But for those who are selfish, who refuse the truth and follow what is wrong, there will be anger and fury.
There will be trouble and pain for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, and also for the Greek.
But glory, honour and peace will come to everyone who does good, first to the Jew, and also to the Greek.
For God does not favour one person over another.
All who sin without having the law will also die without the law. All who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
It is not those who hear the law who are right with God. It is those who do what the law says who will be declared right.
When people of the nations, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law for themselves, even though they do not have the law.
They show that what the law requires is written on their hearts. Their conscience also speaks up, and their thoughts sometimes accuse them and sometimes defend them.
This will happen on the day when God judges people's secrets through Jesus Christ, as my good news declares.
Now you call yourself a Jew. You rely on the law and boast about your relationship with God.
You know his will and approve of what is right, because you are taught by the law.
You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for those in the dark,
a corrector of the foolish and a teacher of little children, because you have in the law the full form of knowledge and truth.
You, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
You who say people must not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who hate idols, do you rob temples?
You who boast in the law, do you dishonour God by breaking the law?
As the Scriptures say, "God's name is spoken against among the nations because of you."
Circumcision has value if you obey the law. But if you break the law, your circumcision has become no circumcision at all.
So if a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will he not be regarded as if he were circumcised?
The man who is not circumcised physically, yet obeys the law, will judge you who have the written code and circumcision but break the law.
A person is not a true Jew if he is only one outwardly. True circumcision is not only something done to the body.
A person is a true Jew if he is one inwardly. True circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a person's praise comes not from people, but from God.
